payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict: CONFORMANT. No findings were recorded during the run.

End state, measured by me after the last placement against each live placement frame:
- u_brown is 0.0024 m off (tolerance 0.01).
- u_orange is 0.0022 m off (tolerance 0.02).
- line_green is 0.0108 m off (tolerance 0.015).
- inverted_u_yellow is 0.0029 m off (tolerance 0.012).
- All orientation errors are 3.1 deg or less (tolerance 10 deg).
- base1 moved 0.0021 m in total.
- All five bystanders are at their initial poses, within 0.0001 m.

How the run was watched. Stationarity monitors stood over every inactive object (the five bystanders, base1, and each task part outside its own span) for the whole run and never fired. While each part was being handled, a clamp-effort monitor and an in-hand slip monitor covered it. Peak efforts were 52.8, 59.4, 15.0 and 82.6 against limits of 100, 200, 170 and 250. Lift heights were 0.2 m or more (u_orange is proven ≥0.105 m from my own measurement). After lift, every part tracked the TCP to within 0.0015 m. All 12 steps matched the expected process, so there were no unplanned steps.

Things that looked suspicious and why I judged them within bounds:
(1) place_line_green. Above its seat, line_green struck an obstruction about 3 cm up, most likely an upright of the already-seated u_brown or u_orange (both named in the step's object_ids as mating parts). It rolled about 22 deg in the fingers and was pushed 0.0183 m up relative to the TCP as the TCP finished descending. On release it dropped in, 0.0109 m off in y. The positional shift is under grasp_slip_tolerance_m (0.02), and the seat error is under its 0.015 tolerance. The neighbouring seated parts moved only about 0.001 m. So no clause failed. The registry gives no bound on in-hand rotation, so that rotation was not judged.
(2) Grasp width. The widths are the executor's reported values. I could not compute width independently without the RG2 calibration table. Finger-joint angle, effort plateau and the part tracking the TCP rule out an air grasp.
(3) Base thresholds. The 0.02 m threshold for base1/base2 is the parts' disturbance_tolerance_m. Neither base has a registry entry of its own, so that threshold is not registry-verified.

Workspace. A camera-depth monitor watched the bench for the whole run (agent-chosen thresholds, used only to trigger looks). It caught an unlisted orange-red cube that appeared at world (0.08, -0.38) during pick_u_orange (observation obs-001-1dc1ec33, looks 0004 and 0005). It stayed there untouched and disturbed nothing, so it has no requirement impact. All other camera fires were explained by the arm's own motion or by expected part placements.

The executor's 'completed' claim agrees with my independent measurement.
